correctness.rationale: In the eight possible binary approval vectors, a single-candidate Pareto-dominance swap forbids an omitted full type above selected lower types, a selected zero type below omitted nonzero types, and an omitted pair p_j opposite a selected singleton e_i for i ≠ j. Thus either the unweighted sum scores support every selected candidate, or an omitted pair p_j plus a selected singleton force all selected singletons to be e_j and all omitted pairs p_j. The fixed weight (2 on j, 1 on others) makes all selected candidates top-score, accounting for ties and multiplicity. Every positive linear-score maximizer is PO and, by the hypersimplex convex hull, fractionally PO; fractional PO trivially implies integral PO. The included deterministic exact checker passed all 6,561 candidate-type capacity profiles with each capacity at most two and 400 larger profiles, totaling 1,620,453 utility-profile comparisons. These computations are finite stress tests, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The statement is a universal four-vector certificate for every unrestricted binary-approval election with at most three voters. The general fPO weighted characterization does not logically imply that all integral PO are fPO on this domain, still less that four election-independent vectors suffice; both implications are proved here. Schünke studies interval-domain structure and broader unrestricted problems, with no equivalent theorem in the inspected relevant portions. The directly relevant Becker et al. full text remains unavailable: priority risk is explicitly retained. An earlier sparse-ballot result bounds approvals per voter, not the number of voters, and does not cover unrestricted approval sets with three voters.

value.rationale: A constant-size universal support family for arbitrary numbers of candidates and committee sizes is a structural solution, not a finite census or score renaming. It completely equates integral and fractional Pareto efficiency on all unrestricted three-voter unit-approval profiles and yields a direct O(m log m) certificate. The domain allows every binary approval type and unbounded repetitions; the three-pair approval instance escapes both interval-domain simplifications. It supplies a natural boundary case of a recent open efficiency-structure problem.
